key_insight: A quasi-square spanwise wall-oscillation waveform exposes two phases that alternately restart or suppress the turbulent self-sustaining process, revealing how drag reduction is controlled by Stokes-strain timing.
engineering_relevance: Temporally redistributing wall oscillation can improve drag reduction beyond a sinusoidal baseline, offering a practical control knob for turbulent channel-flow management.
method: DNS of turbulent channel flow at friction Reynolds number ~200
Spanwise wall actuation with quasi-square-wave forcing
evidence_signal: The study reports a 2.5 percentage-point increase in gross drag-reduction margin over the optimal sinusoidal case, supported by phase-resolved flow observations and governing-equation-level enstrophy budgets.
watch_item: The result is demonstrated in DNS at Re_tau around 200, so performance and implementation complexity may change at higher Reynolds numbers or in hardware with limited actuation fidelity.
paper_title: Duty-cycle modulation of the self-sustaining process by spanwise wall oscillation
